standard_prerequisites.name: The cup product is functorial, so maps of complexes in the category of differential graded modules give a commutative diagram whose columns are distinguished triangles
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns a distinguished triangle of complexes into a relation between the products occurring in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: A bounded below complex sits in a distinguished triangle with its truncation above a degree and the degree piece, and the truncation has fewer nonzero terms
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the induction that reduces the first complex to a single degree.

standard_prerequisites.name: The statement is of a degreewise nature, so vanishing of the two sides in low degrees lets one replace a bounded below complex by a bounded piece
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the same reduction for the second complex, after which only the single degree case is left.

core_obligations: Recall the notation for the category of differential graded modules over the two spaces and record that the cup product is functorial: a map of complexes gives a commutative diagram, and a distinguished triangle gives distinguished triangles in the columns (proof lines 6394-6427).

If the first complex vanishes below a degree, cut it by the termwise split exact sequence into its truncation above that degree and the single degree piece, obtaining a distinguished triangle, and conclude that it suffices to treat both pieces separately (proof lines 6428-6443).

Finish the reduction for the first complex by induction on the number of nonzero terms, so that it may be assumed to be concentrated in one degree; this uses that the truncation has fewer nonzero terms (proof lines 6440-6443).

In the single degree case use the base change statement to see that the first cohomology has finite tor dimension, say in degrees between i and j, and choose an integer N far above (proof lines 6445-6455).

Cut the second complex by the distinguished triangle with its truncation and its low piece; since both products have vanishing cohomology in degrees at most N plus i, the statement in any fixed degree may be proved after replacing the second complex by a bounded piece (proof lines 6456-6485).
Repeat the same argument once more to reduce the second complex to a single degree as well, and conclude with the single sheaf statement (proof lines 6486-6495).
proof_roadmap: Record functoriality of the cup product on distinguished triangles (proof lines 6394-6427).
Reduce the first complex to one degree by truncation and induction (proof lines 6428-6443).
Control the degrees with the tor amplitude of the first cohomology and cut the second complex (proof lines 6445-6485).
Reduce the second complex to one degree and apply the single sheaf case (proof lines 6486-6495).
difficulty_reason: 证明 102 行、是标准的「两次归纳」结构：先用杯积的函子性把 distinguished triangle 搬到题面两张复形上，再对第一个复形用截断 + 归纳归约到单一度数；单度数情形先用基变换结果算出上同调有限 tor 维数，再对第二个复形做同样的截断论证（靠「两侧在低度数消没」把问题压到固定度数），最后把单度数情形交给单层引理。承重步骤（函子性、两次截断、度数控制）都写在 span 内；5 处引用里 2 处同章、3 处跨章，作导航桩。
